2026-11-16.title: Monday of the Thirty-third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: You have abandoned the love you had at first
Those who are victorious I will feed from the tree of life
2026-11-16.alt: Optional memorials: St Margaret of Scotland; St Gertrude, virgin.
2026-11-16.verse: Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight; your faith has saved you.”
theo: In the last weeks of the year the first readings come from the Book of Revelation. The risen Christ speaks to the church of Ephesus, praising its hard work and endurance, but with one complaint: “you have abandoned the love you had at first”. A community can be orthodox and busy and still have grown cold. The remedy: remember, repent, and do the works you did at first.

Near Jericho a blind beggar hears that Jesus is passing and cries out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” The crowd tells him to be quiet; he shouts all the more. Jesus stops and asks, “What do you want me to do for you?” “Lord, let me see again.” He receives his sight and follows Jesus, glorifying God. Persistent prayer, a clear request, and a life of following: this is how first love is recovered.
outline: Ask: when was your love for Jesus warmest? What has changed?
The blind man would not be silenced.
Remember, repent, do the first works.
live: Recall one practice from a time of fervour and take it up again.
Tell Jesus plainly today what you want him to do for you.
2026-11-16.prayer: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me. Open my eyes, rekindle the love I had at first, and let me follow you on the way, glorifying God. Amen.

quick: A busy church can lose its first love.
Cry out, even when others tell you to be quiet.
2026-11-16.action: Take up again one practice from a time of fervour.
2026-11-16.question: Have I lost the love I had at first?

homily: Dear friends, in these last weeks of the year the Church reads the Book of Revelation. Today the risen Christ speaks to the church of Ephesus. He praises its hard work and endurance, but he has one complaint: you have abandoned the love you had at first (Revelation 2:4). A community can be correct and busy and still have grown cold.

The remedy is threefold: remember from where you have fallen, repent, and do the works you did at first (Revelation 2:5). Remember the joy of your First Communion, your wedding day, your first steps in prayer. Love is renewed by returning to its source.

Near Jericho a blind beggar hears that Jesus is passing by and cries out: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me! The crowd tells him to be quiet, and he cries out all the more. Jesus asks: what do you want me to do for you? Lord, let me see again (Luke 18:38–41).

Let us make his prayer our own: Lord, let me see. Let me see where my love has cooled, and let me see you again as I saw you at first. And when we see, let us do what the blind man did: follow him, glorifying God. Amen.
kids: Children, the blind man shouted to Jesus and did not stop. Jesus heard him! Pray today: Jesus, help me to see you in everyone.

intro: Cry out, return to first love, ask for sight and follow.

sub: The blind man heard Jesus passing.
The crowd tried to silence him.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Then he shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
points.apply: Pray the Jesus Prayer often today.

sub: Ephesus worked hard but grew cold.
q: Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem, Thus says the LORD: I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride, how you followed me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.
But I have this against you, that you have abandoned the love you had at first. Remember then from what you have fallen; repent, and do the works you did at first.
points.apply: Take up one practice of your first fervour.

q: Open my eyes, so that I may behold wondrous things out of your law.
“What do you want me to do for you?” He said, “Lord, let me see again.” Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight; your faith has saved you.”
points.apply: Ask Jesus plainly for what you need.
